IX.}}</noinclude>vvere scales, and he receiued sight. and rising he vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Paul also him self, though vvith the diuine and heauenly voice prostrated and instructed, yet vvas sent to a man to receiue the Sacraments, & to be ioyned to the Church. ''August. de doct. Chr. lib. 1. in proœm''.}}∷ baptized. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=19}}† And vvhen he had taken meate, he vvas strengthened.

And he vvas vvith the disciples that vvere at Damascus, for certaine daies. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=20}}† And incontinent entring into the synagogs, he preached {{sc|Iesvs}}, that this is the sonne of God. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=21}}† And al that heard, vvere astonied, and said, Is not this he that expugned in Hierusalem those that inuocated this name: and came hither to this purpose that he might bring them bound to the cheefe priests? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=22}}† But Saul vvaxed mightie much more, and confounded the Ievves that dvvelt at Damascus, affirming that this is {{sc|Christ}}.⊣ {{verse|chapter=9|verse=23}}† And vvhen many daies vvere passed, the Ievves consulted that they might kil him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=24}}† But their conspiracie came to Sauls knovvledge. And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Cor. 11, 32.''}}* they kept the gates also day and night, that they might kil him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=25}}† But the disciples taking him in the night, conueied him avvay by the vvall, letting him dovvne in a basket.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=26}}† And vvhen he vvas come into Hierusalem, he assaied to ioyne him self to the disciples, & al feared him, not beleeuing that he vvas a disciple. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=27}}† But Barnabas tooke him & brought him to the Apostles, and told them hovv in the vvay he had seen our Lord, and that he spake vnto him, and hovv in Damascus he dealt confidently in the name of {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=28}}† And he vvas vvith them going in and going out in Hierusalem, and dealing confidently in the name of our Lord. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=29}}† He spake also to the Gentiles, and disputed vvith the Greekes: but they sought to kil him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=30}}† Vvhich vvhen the brethren had knovven, they brought him dovvne to Cæsaréa, and sent him avvay to Tarsus.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=31}}† The {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Church visibly procedeth still vvith much comfort & manifold increase euen by persecution.}}∷ {{sc|Chvrch}} truely through al Ievvrie & Galilee and Samaria had peace, & vvas edified, vvalking in the feare of our Lord, and vvas replenished vvith the consolation of the holy Ghost.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=32}}† And it came to passe, that Peter as he passed through al, came to the saincts that dvvelt at Lydda. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=33}}† and he found there a certaine man named Æneas, lying in his bed from eight yeres before, vvho had the palsey. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=34}}† And Peter said to him, Æneas, our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`healeth''.}}`heale' thee: arise, and make thy bed. And incontinent he arose. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=35}}† And al that dvvelt at Lydda and Saróna, savv him: vvho conuerted to our Lord.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
